featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great experience at Stur Fry Box in Infiniti Mall. The concept of customizable Asian meal bowls is fantastic — I went with the Bombay Chicken Chili Bowl and it was delicious, spicy, and satisfying. The portion size was generous for the price, and the ingredients tasted fresh.

The service was quick and the staff was friendly. I also tried the bubble tea — a nice bonus if you’re into something sweet and refreshing with your meal.

Only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that the seating area can get crowded during peak hours and the food could be served slightly hotter.

Overall, a solid spot for quick, flavorful Asian food. Definitely worth a visit if you’re at the mall!

featured_reviews.name: SUDHANSHU
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food was quite average, and the service was extremely poor. The servers lacked basic courtesy while communicating with us. A starter was suggested by the server, but it was disappointing and we couldn’t finish it. When we requested it to be packed, we were told it wouldn’t be done as it was already half eaten.
We then asked for a box so we could pack it ourselves, but instead were handed a small silver plastic bag. Imagine being expected to pack your own food at the table, using a small spoon, into a plastic bag.
If packing leftover food was not possible, that’s understandable, but the way it was communicated was highly inappropriate. Eventually, we had to somehow finish the remaining food as we didn’t want it to go to waste. Overall, a very disappointing experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We ordered had veg manchow soup from Flavours of China Restaurant, and to our shock, we found a thin metal wire inside it. This was an extremely dangerous and unacceptable experience. My parents were having the soup, and it could have caused a serious health issue or injury if they had accidentally swallowed it.
Thankfully, they noticed it in time but this kind of negligence is inexcusable. We expect much higher safety and hygiene standards, especially from food establishments. I hope the restaurant takes this feedback seriously and investigates how such a hazardous item ended up in the food.
Extremely disappointed and concerned. Please be cautious if you're ordering from here.

featured_reviews.review_text:

So FOC lollipop is their special lollipop which costs around 350/- (100/- extra than normal lollipop) and it's worth paying, that green masala tastes so good and it makes the lollipop juicy.
Chicken crispy was normal like you'll get it in any other restaurant but with less spices.

I personally liked it. but I cannot guarantee that everyone will like it. cuz it was very unique in taste and really heavy, you cannot finish it by yourself.

The place is nice, clean. The service is good. They don't take longer to cook your food.
interior is good. and love the way they cook the food, less masalas, well clocked , less spices and unique flavors.

They only had 2 options for dessert... 😅
caramel custard and rabdi, that's it.
top floor is quite but stairs are very small. hard to walk on those steps seriously. They need to do something about it else someone will definitely fall from those. Place is not easily noticable. It is in my locality but I was not knowing about this place.
there's parking for bikes but no parking for cars.
and yes it is not their own parking. it's just a small road everyone's parking their two wheelers.

I'll try other dishes too... they really had some serious flavors...🤟🏻

featured_reviews.name: A-di
featured_reviews.review_text:
After reading several reviews, I decided to visit this restaurant—easily located with the help of Google Maps.

It’s a small place tucked into a lane, nicely lit with a dark, cozy ambiance. The staff seemed friendly and welcoming. I checked with them and ordered their specialty: Chicken 1000 Rice.

The presentation stood out—the dish was served on a large plate rather than in a traditional serving bowl with gravy. Taste-wise, it was good. The chicken was tender, and the rice was perfectly cooked—not too hard or overdone.

However, the overall flavor felt a bit bland, like something was missing. Thankfully, their Schezwan sauce saved the day—thick, flavorful, and really elevated the dish.

📍 If you’re around Dadar, it’s worth a visit.
💧 Small tip: Don’t forget to buy bottled drinking water.

• Huge waste of time

Would not recommend, especially if you're hungry or short on time. Very disappointing experience. 👎

featured_reviews.name: Yash Karaday
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours of China in Lalbaugh serves up some tasty Chinese dishes, but there are a few things to consider before visiting. First off, parking is a significant issue. The area is quite congested, and finding a spot can be a frustrating experience, especially during peak hours. If you’re planning to drive, I’d recommend allowing extra time just to park.

Once inside, the restaurant is noticeably loud and crowded. The place is popular, which is great, but it also means that the noise level can be quite high, making conversation difficult. The seating is a bit cramped, adding to the bustling atmosphere. If you’re looking for a quiet, relaxing dining experience, this might not be the best choice.

On the positive side, the food is flavorful, and the portions are generous. The menu offers a wide variety of Chinese dishes, and the service is relatively quick despite the crowd. If you don’t mind the noise and the parking hassle, Flavours of China is a decent option for a casual meal.

Each bite offers a perfect textural contrast between the crispy, tender Manchurian balls and the fragrant, vegetable-loaded fried rice that soaks up the spicy gravy beautifully. It’s an irresistible, standout fusion dish that turns a simple meal into an absolute feast for the taste buds."

featured_reviews.name: Prithu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Royal China is the kind of place that makes you feel underdressed even when you are dressed well.

The ambience is classy without trying too hard, dim lighting, elegant interiors, and the sort of atmosphere where people suddenly start speaking 20 percent softer. It has that proper fine dining energy where even the water arrives looking expensive.

The food absolutely holds up to the reputation. The menu is extensive, packed with authentic Chinese dishes that actually taste refined instead of just aggressively spicy. The dim sums are a standout, and the overall quality of ingredients is noticeable from the first bite itself.

Service is polished and attentive without hovering over your table every two minutes asking if “everything is okay.” They know what they are doing, which makes the whole experience feel smooth.

Yes, it is expensive. The bill arrives with enough confidence to remind you this is not your local takeaway spot. But unlike many overpriced fine dining places, this one at least gives you the feeling that your money went somewhere meaningful.

Final verdict: Elegant, reliable, and consistently good. Come for the food, stay for the feeling of temporarily having your life together.

featured_reviews.name: Sweet Sour
featured_reviews.review_text:
For lovers of authentic Chinese cuisine, Royal China offers a refined and memorable dining experience, combining elegant ambiance with thoughtfully curated flavors.

I began with their mocktails — the Jade Green Cooler and Pearl of the Orient. Both were beautifully presented and refreshingly balanced, with subtle yet distinct flavor profiles that made them perfect palate openers.

The starters truly set the tone for the meal. The Spicy Lotus Root stood out with its crisp texture and bold seasoning, delivering a satisfying crunch in every bite. The Crispy Silken Tofu with Sweet Chilli Sauce was equally impressive — delicately crisp on the outside while remaining soft and silky within, complemented by a flavorful sweet and mildly spicy glaze.

Moving on to the main course, the Burnt Chilli Garlic Noodles were rich, aromatic, and packed with deep, smoky flavors that lingered pleasantly. Paired with this were the Steamed Wontons in Spicy Sauce, which were light yet indulgent, coated in a well-balanced sauce that added just the right amount of heat without overpowering the dish.

The experience concluded on a decadent note with the Chocolate Dome dessert — a visually stunning and indulgent creation that perfectly balanced richness and sweetness, making it a delightful end to the meal.

Overall, Royal China stands out as a sophisticated destination for those seeking high-quality Chinese cuisine, where each dish is crafted with attention to detail and flavor harmony.

I recently visited Royal China and the experience was amazing. The place has a very classy and elegant vibe. The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, which made the visit even better.
We started with Orange Blossom, a refreshing mocktail full of fruity flavours of orange, cranberry, and apple. The Yuzu Viking was another favourite with pineapple juice and elderflower syrup, very light and fresh.
For starters, the Belgian Pork Dumplings were soft, flavourful, and perfectly steamed. The Smoked Shredded Chicken was crispy, garlicky, and had a nice crunch from the vegetables.
The highlight for me was the Truffle Tenderloin, seared to perfection and served on a sizzling plate with that rich truffle aroma. The Hong Kong Street Style Noodles were simple yet very tasty, with beansprouts and spring onion adding the right crunch.
We ended with the Chocolate Dome, which was a delightful surprise with mud cake and ice cream inside. Overall, Royal China is definitely a place I would recommend for anyone who enjoys great food, a classy setting, and excellent service.

featured_reviews.review_text:
​If you are looking for high-quality Pan-Asian cuisine in the Andheri/Sakinaka area, Asia Kitchen remains one of the most reliable spots. It manages to balance a sophisticated dining atmosphere with a menu that feels both authentic and approachable.
​The Ambiance
The decor is modern and sleek, making it equally suitable for a formal business lunch or a relaxed dinner with family.
​The Food
The menu is a well-curated journey through Chinese, Japanese, and Southeast Asian flavors. Some standout highlights include:
​Dim Sums: The crust is consistently delicate, and the fillings—especially the Truffle Edamame—are flavorful and fresh.
​Sushi: For those who enjoy Japanese, the Salmon and Avocado rolls are well-constructed and use high-grade ingredients.
​Main Course: The Chicken Thai Green Curry is aromatic and perfectly balanced, pairing beautifully with Jasmine rice. Their signature Szechuan Noodles offer that classic fiery kick without being overwhelming.
​The Service
The staff is generally attentive and well-versed in the menu. They are happy to provide recommendations based on your spice tolerance and dietary preferences, which adds a personalized touch to the meal.
​The Verdict
While it sits at a slightly higher price point than your average local eatery, the consistency in taste and the upscale environment justify the cost. It’s a great pick for anyone in Mumbai wanting a dependable, delicious Asian feast.
​Pro Tip: It can get quite busy on weekend evenings, so booking a table in advance is highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited China Bistro in BKC with my family for the first time as we were craving authentic Chinese cuisine, and the experience was genuinely impressive. Located in the posh BKC area of Mumbai, the restaurant has a premium fine-dining vibe with a well-curated menu and a great ambience for family dinners, friend gatherings, or even a date night.

They also offer Gold and Platinum meal packages with options including soups, dim sums, appetizers, mains, desserts, mocktails, and even alcohol packages with beer, wine, whiskey, and gin selections. However, we preferred ordering dishes individually.

Being vegetarians, we explored their veg menu:

⭐ Singaporean Crispy Lotus Root – Easily the highlight of our meal. Perfectly crispy lotus root tossed with honey and curry leaves with amazing flavor balance. One of their specials and absolutely worth trying.
Rating: 5/5

⭐ Crunchy Avocado Sushi Roll (Jain) – Fresh, crunchy, and delicious with avocado, mayo, and tanuki. Their sushi selection is definitely worth exploring.
Rating: 4/5

⭐ Vegetable Spring Roll – Crispy, flavorful, and served perfectly hot.
Rating: 4.5/5

⭐ Singapore Veg Noodles – Nicely cooked with curry oil, assorted vegetables, and chili. Comforting and flavorful without being too overpowering.
Rating: 4/5

⭐ Tropical Summer Bubble Tea – A refreshing summer drink with mango, strawberry, ice cream, milk, and boba pearls. Quite unique and enjoyable.
Rating: 4/5

They also have Korean stone pots, cocktails, and a good dessert variety which we couldn’t try this time. Service was smooth, valet parking was conveniently arranged, and the staff was polite and attentive.

The pricing is definitely on the higher side, but considering the location, ambience, and authentic flavors, it feels justified if you enjoy premium dining experiences and want to try something different.

Overall Rating: 4.5/5

featured_reviews.name: Tejaswi Sankhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
**5 Spice, Saki Naka – Review (300 words)**

5 Spice at Saki Naka, Mumbai, is a popular go-to spot for lovers of Indo-Chinese cuisine with a twist of comfort food indulgence. Nestled in a bustling part of the city, this branch of the well-known 5 Spice chain offers a consistent dining experience, both in terms of flavor and portion size.

The ambience is casual yet inviting, with dim lighting and comfortable seating. It’s not overly fancy, but clean and functional – perfect for casual dining with friends, family, or even a quick solo meal. Service is generally prompt, though peak hours can result in slight delays.

The menu is extensive, covering everything from classic starters like Chicken Lollipop and Paneer Chilly to overloaded mains such as Burnt Garlic Fried Rice, Thai Pot Rice, and their signature gravies like Hot Garlic Sauce or Sapo Chicken. Portions are huge, often enough to share between two hungry diners. Vegetarian and non-vegetarian options are both well represented.

One of the major highlights is their dessert selection. The *Death by Chocolate* is a crowd favorite – a decadent, towering mix of chocolate cake, brownie, ice cream, and sauce – not for the faint-hearted or light eaters. It’s rich, heavy, and pure indulgence.

Prices are on the higher side compared to street Chinese joints, but justified by the generous portions and quality of ingredients. Hygiene standards are commendable.

In summary, 5 Spice in Saki Naka lives up to its brand reputation: hearty meals, big servings, flavorful sauces, and comfort food done right. It's not gourmet or cutting-edge, but if you're craving satisfying Indo-Chinese in a cozy setting, it delivers exactly what you’d expect – and a bit more. Just make sure to go with an appetite and maybe a friend to share that dessert!

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Tondwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
5spice is known for its Asian cuisine mainly chinese. They have many good options especially in starters and desserts.  The main course is quiet appetizing too.

For food quality, I would say that it is okay. Sometimes I have had bad experiences as well, where the meat had some stale smell and taste, but most often the food is well cooked and the taste is just fine.

I would say that for two people, one main course is more than enough. The prices is on the expensive side but you can say that you get your food’s worth for sure.

This specific outlet had top and underground floor. But now the top floor has gone for some renovation.

There is valet parking available which is free. So that is nice.

For desserts they have some really nice options right from rocky road, mission impossible and death by chocolate. One must definitely try their Mission impossible and Death by chocolate cake.  The dessert serving sizes are quiet huge so be sure you have sufficient stomach space left after main course in order to be able to finish the whole dessert.

I would not say that they have the best food but one can definitely good quantity and decent chinese food.  I would rate this place and overall 7/10.

Point worth noting here is that they charge 7.5% service charge over and above food cost and GST. But yes, the price is worth what you get here for sure.
